name: Janaki Mandir

hotspots.name: Dedicated to Sita
hotspots.details: Janaki Mandir is dedicated to Goddess Sita, also called Janaki. The revered image of Sita is within the sanctum; this exterior model does not document its interior.

hotspots.name: Queen Vrisha Bhanu
hotspots.details: Queen Vrisha Bhanu of Tikamgarh commissioned the temple. Sources differ on completion: Nepal Tourism Board gives 1910, while Nepal Views gives 1911; an exact 1895 start is not asserted here.

hotspots.name: Hindu, Mughal and Rajput traditions
hotspots.details: The temple combines Koiri-Hindu, Mughal and Rajput architectural traditions, according to Nepal Tourism Board.

hotspots.name: Mughal-influenced domes
hotspots.details: The domes are described as Mughal-style in Nepal Views. The procedural saffron and white finish shown here is illustrative, not a measured record of historic paint.

hotspots.name: Rajasthani jharokhas
hotspots.details: Rajasthani jharokhas—overhanging balconies—are among the architectural features identified in the temple by Nepal Views.

hotspots.name: Carved pillars
hotspots.details: Nepal Views describes the temple as having intricately carved artistic pillars. This digital model preserves the creator’s modeled exterior detail.

hotspots.name: Stone and marble
hotspots.details: Nepal Tourism Board describes Janaki Mandir as built from stone and marble. Its cream-white procedural finish is an artistic rendering treatment.

hotspots.name: Sixty main rooms
hotspots.details: Nepal Views reports 60 main rooms in the temple. This label provides building context; the rendered exterior does not expose or enumerate those rooms.

hotspots.name: Janakpurdham, Mithila
hotspots.details: The temple stands in Janakpur, in Nepal’s eastern Terai and Mithila cultural region. The Ramayana tradition associates Janakpur with King Janak and Sita.

hotspots.name: Nau Lakha Mandir
hotspots.details: The temple is popularly called Nau Lakha Mandir. The name is traditionally connected with a construction cost of nine lakh; sources differ on the currency and the account is treated as tradition.

hotspots.name: Vivah Panchami
hotspots.details: Vivah Panchami commemorates the marriage of Rama and Sita. Janakpur celebrates it with rituals, processions and devotional performances in November–December.

hotspots.name: Rama and Sita tradition
hotspots.details: The adjacent Vivah Mandap is traditionally associated with the divine wedding of Rama and Sita. This contextual label does not identify a separate marriage pavilion in the source model.
